# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code when working in this repository.

## What this is

**__PROJECT_NAME__** — a TypeScript project bootstrapped by
[m3l-groundwork](https://github.com/monte3l/m3l-groundwork). This baseline
is deliberately generic: it holds for any TypeScript project regardless of
domain. Run `/customize` to tailor it to what you're actually building.

## Tech Stack

TypeScript, `strict: true`, ESM only (`"type": "module"`), compiled with
`tsc` — no bundler by default. Package manager: `pnpm`. Node 24+ only
(`.node-version` is the authority; `check:node-version` gates drift).

## Commands

Run any task with `pnpm <script>`.

| Script                         | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pnpm build`                   | `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json` — emits `dist/`                                                                                                                                                             |
| `pnpm typecheck`               | `tsc -b --force` over the tooling project (src + tests)                                                                                                                                                  |
| `pnpm lint`                    | ESLint over the whole repo                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `pnpm format` / `format:check` | Prettier write / check                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `pnpm test` / `test:coverage`  | Vitest, with or without the coverage gate                                                                                                                                                                |
| `pnpm knip`                    | Unused-dependency / unused-export hygiene; a `verify` step. `knip.json` ignores `@commitlint/config-conventional` and `@commitlint/types`, which are loaded by a string and a JSDoc type knip cannot see |
| `pnpm check:exports`           | publint + are-the-types-wrong against a packed tarball                                                                                                                                                   |
| `pnpm check:node-version`      | `.node-version` is authoritative; forbids a hardcoded pin in CI                                                                                                                                          |
| `pnpm verify`                  | Every gate above plus the `harness`/`toolchain` graders, in `verify-steps.mjs` order; CI runs them as five parallel group lanes                                                                          |
| `pnpm prepare`                 | Installs the lefthook git hooks                                                                                                                                                                          |

Run `pnpm verify` before considering any task done — it reproduces CI
locally.

## Git Workflow

**Conventional Commits (required)**, enforced by the `commit-msg` hook
(`bin/lint-commit.mjs`, run after `bin/strip-claude-trailers.mjs` removes
harness-injected `Claude-*` trailers). Add a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer when Claude
authored or substantially assisted a commit — see `.claude/skills/writing-commits/`.

Branch off `main` as `feat/<slug>` / `fix/<slug>`, never work directly on
`main` — `guard-branch-isolation.mjs` blocks `src/**`/`tests/**` writes
while `HEAD` is `main`. Land any `src/`/`tests/` change via PR. Run
`.claude/skills/starting-work/` before beginning change-work if you haven't
already settled the branch and PR decision.

Never `git push --force` a shared branch.

## Architecture & Decisions

`src/index.ts` is the current public entry point (see the `exports` map in
`package.json`). By convention, anything under `src/internal/` (if you create
it) is private and is not re-exported from the entry point; no lint rule
enforces this, so review for it.

## Agent Operating Model

**Hub-and-spoke**: the hub plans and dispatches to spokes, and never writes
`src/`/test code itself — enforced by `.claude/hooks/guard-hub-src-writes.mjs`
and `disallowedTools: Agent` on every spoke. For a piece of work with a clear
contract:

1. `test-author` writes failing tests from the contract (RED phase), and
   confirms they fail for the right reason.
2. `code-implementer` makes them pass with the minimal correct
   implementation, then refactors while green (GREEN phase).
3. Read-only review spokes (`code-reviewer` always; `silent-failure-hunter`
   when the diff has error-handling paths) run in parallel over the diff.
   Must-fix findings route back to `code-implementer`, and the loop repeats
   until clean.

Also shipped: `.claude/agents/Explore.md`, a fast read-only search agent for
locating files and symbols.

Skills, each in `.claude/skills/<name>/`:

- `starting-work` — pre-work gate: picks the branch and whether a PR is needed.
- `writing-commits` — drafts a Conventional Commit from the staged diff.
- `creating-prs` — verifies gates, pushes, opens the PR and picks a merge path.
- `triaging-ci` — diagnoses a failed CI run and proposes fixes.
- `finishing-work` — post-merge cleanup: branches, refs, work log.
- `typescript-guidance` / `harness-guidance` — live research and refresh
  sweeps (see Freshness).

**The guard also screens `Bash`, but only conservatively.** The same hook
blocks a `Bash` command that visibly writes into `src/` or `tests/` (redirects,
`tee`, `sed -i`, `cp`/`mv` into them, an interpreter snippet that writes there,
a copy, move or removal of a parent of `src/` such as `rm -rf .`) unless the caller is
`test-author` or `code-implementer`. It cannot catch an indirect write (a
script from a project file, an `eval`, a computed path, a build step, a
formatter or fixer, `git rm`/`git mv`, `tar`/`curl -o`), so hub-and-spoke is a
convention backed by a guard that raises the bar, not a proof. To override it
deliberately, run the command yourself with the `!` prefix at the Claude Code
prompt, or edit the hook's registration in `.claude/settings.json`.

**Managed settings and mods can silently disable the guards.** A managed
deployment (`managed-settings.json`, MDM, a console policy) outranks every file
here, and `allowManagedHooksOnly` runs only managed hooks. An installed mod
that handles `tool.check` can approve a call a project `PreToolUse` hook
blocked, unless managed settings or a Team or Enterprise `/login` is in use. Nothing in the repo can detect
either: on a machine you don't control, check `/status` ("Setting sources") and
`/plugin` before trusting `guard-hub-src-writes.mjs` and
`guard-branch-isolation.mjs`. Detail and sources:
`.claude/rules/agent-dispatch.md`.

**The guard keys on `agent_id` as well as `agent_type`.** A call counts as a
writer spoke only with both present, so one carrying `agent_type` alone is
treated as the hub and blocked, as is a fork subagent unless its payload
reports a writer `agent_type` with an `agent_id` (details and versions in
`.claude/rules/agent-dispatch.md`). An in-process
agent-teams teammate has a documented `agent_id`, so one built from a writer
definition that reports that `agent_type` would pass.

**Four guards block when they fail, and a secrets deny rule ships in
`settings.json`.** `guard-secret-writes`, `guard-hub-src-writes`,
`guard-branch-isolation` and `guard-protected-paths` carry
`"onFailure": "block"` (Claude Code 2.1.295 or later): a hook that cannot
start, times out, exits with any code other than 0 or 2, or prints invalid
JSON blocks the call instead of letting it through. Each guard still handles
bad input itself and exits 0 on purpose. Because `guard-hub-src-writes` is also
on `Bash`, a missing `node` blocks every `Bash` call until fixed (run the
command with the `!` prefix to get past it). The style guards and
`guard-git-push-signed` stay fail-open on purpose: the push guard has its own
parser and the remote's signed-commit rule is the authoritative layer.
`permissions.deny` blocks reading `.env`, `.env.*`, `secrets/`,
`credentials.json` and `secrets.yaml` (which also covers `cat`, `head` and
`tail` on them in `Bash`) and editing `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `package-lock.json`,
`yarn.lock` and the repository's `.git/` directory. It does not cover `grep -r`,
a script that opens the file itself, a subprocess such as `pnpm install`
rewriting the lock file, or a linked worktree, where `.git` is a file.

**A spoke's `permissionMode` can be overridden.** A session in auto,
`acceptEdits` or `bypassPermissions` mode overrides a spoke's `permissionMode`
(the field applies only in `default`, `dontAsk` or `plan`), so the hooks, not
`permissionMode`, bound a spoke. A subagent can spawn subagents three layers
deep by default; `disallowedTools: Agent` on every spoke keeps the roster flat.

Full dispatch-sizing and recovery guidance: `.claude/rules/agent-dispatch.md`
(auto-loads when editing `.claude/skills/**` or `.claude/agents/**`).

## Coding, errors & tests

Path-scoped rules auto-load on matching files:

- `src/**` → `.claude/rules/src.md`
- `**/tests/**`, `**/*.test.ts` → `.claude/rules/tests.md`
- `src/**`, `**/tests/**` → `.claude/rules/refactoring.md` (behavior-preserving changes)
- `.claude/skills/**`, `.claude/agents/**` → `.claude/rules/agent-dispatch.md`

## Security

Never log secrets, tokens, or caller data. Validate external input at the
public API boundary. `.claude/hooks/guard-secret-writes.mjs` blocks writing
a real secret to disk at edit time; keep it that way rather than relying on
CI to catch it after the fact.

## Definition of Done

`pnpm verify` passes; a public API change carries a Conventional Commit with
the correct semver impact; new/changed exports have TSDoc and tests. If you
touched the harness itself (hooks, agents, skills, rules, `settings.json`),
`pnpm verify`'s `harness` step (`bin/check-harness.mjs`) must stay green: it
fails on broken wiring and only warns on quality.
The `toolchain` step (`bin/check-toolchain.mjs`) runs on every
`pnpm verify`, and must stay green when you touch the TypeScript toolchain
(`tsconfig*.json`, `eslint.config.js`, `vitest.config.ts`,
`bin/lib/verify-steps.mjs`, the toolchain pins in `package.json`) the same way: it fails on wiring `tsc` and ESLint do not catch (a build
project that emits nowhere, a verify step naming a script that does not exist)
and only warns on quality (a missing strict flag, an option TypeScript has
deprecated). Never silence it by deleting the check or lowering a threshold --
fix the config it points at.

## Forbidden Patterns

**Enforced at write time by hooks:** `any` implied by CommonJS constructs
(`require`, `module.exports`, `__dirname`, `__filename`), a missing `.js`
extension on a relative import, a hand-edit to `dist/` or `coverage/`, a
write to `src/`/`tests/` while on `main`, a real secret written to disk,
an unsigned `git push` when `commit.gpgsign` is on, and a `run_in_background`
Bash call stacked with a shell-level detach construct.

**No automated guard — need conscious care:** no `any` in the public API;
never swallow an error silently; no top-level side effects; never
`git push --force`.

## Freshness

This baseline is frozen at the moment `m3l-groundwork` last emitted it. Run
`/customize`'s guidance pass — or `.claude/skills/typescript-guidance/` /
`.claude/skills/harness-guidance/` directly in refresh mode — periodically
to sweep the toolchain and harness against current upstream guidance; its
`gaps` mode recommends tooling the project doesn't have yet. See
`docs/research/typescript-refresh.md` and `docs/research/harness-refresh.md`
for the living trackers.

name: Release

# What this does: on every push to `main`, this workflow either opens a PR
# that bumps the package version and changelog, or -- once that PR has
# merged -- packs and publishes the package to npm. It runs
# [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets), the tool this
# project uses to track pending releases (each PR that changes the
# package's user-facing behavior adds a small Markdown file under
# `.changeset/` describing the change and its version bump; this workflow
# reads those files to decide what to do next).
#
# The flow, one job each:
#   1. select-mode  reads the repo and decides: "version", "publish", or "none"
#   2. version      opens or updates the "Version Packages" PR
#   3. pack         builds, runs every gate, and packs the tarball
#   4. publish      uploads that tarball to npm via trusted publishing
#
# "Trusted publishing" is npm's passwordless publish mechanism: instead of a
# long-lived npm token stored as a secret, this workflow proves its identity
# to npm via OIDC (OpenID Connect -- a short-lived, cryptographically signed
# token GitHub Actions mints for the running job, which npm verifies against
# the trusted-publisher config for this exact repo and workflow file). This
# is the shape the changesets docs recommend for trusted publishing: the one
# job that holds the OIDC token (`publish`, via `id-token: write`) never runs
# build, test, or repo-script code -- it only runs the changesets CLI and the
# pnpm shim below, with `--ignore-scripts`. `pack` holds nothing beyond
# `contents: read`.
#
# "Staged" publish (vs. a "direct" one) means a staged publish uploads the
# tarball and creates the version, but it isn't installable yet until a
# maintainer separately approves it with 2FA (`npm stage approve`) -- npm's
# own stronger default over a direct `npm publish`, which would make the
# version live immediately. "Provenance" is the signed, publicly verifiable
# record npm attaches to a trusted-published package, linking it back to the
# exact commit and workflow run that built it.
#
# npm trusted publishers are configured per package, against this exact file
# name (`release.yml`, not a path) -- see this pack's adoptNotes for the
# one-time setup this depends on.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

# Reset, then grant per job.
permissions: {}

# Releases must not be cancelled midway: a half-published release is worse
# than a queued one.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}

jobs:
  select-mode:
    name: Select mode
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    outputs:
      mode: ${{ steps.select-mode.outputs.mode }}
      publish-plan-artifact-id: ${{ steps.select-mode.outputs.publish-plan-artifact-id }}
    permissions:
      contents: read # actions/checkout
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      # `.node-version` is the single Node pin, so this file must never carry
      # a literal version (see check-node-version.mjs). No package-manager
      # cache anywhere in this file: a restored cache is an input an attacker
      # can poison, and these jobs are the ones that publish.
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@73e46992e05b19abd31f2f3c20e0e7370d762115 # v6.1.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - id: select-mode
        uses: changesets/action/select-mode@ae32849d5ba541f9ae29e40e22a623bc13562f51 # v2

  version:
    name: Open version PR
    needs: select-mode
    if: needs.select-mode.outputs.mode == 'version'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read # actions/checkout; see below for who does the actual writing
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@73e46992e05b19abd31f2f3c20e0e7370d762115 # v6.1.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      # If this project's branch protection requires status checks on every
      # PR with no bypass actor, a PR opened with the default GITHUB_TOKEN
      # never triggers `pull_request`-event workflows (GitHub's own
      # anti-recursion rule) and could therefore never merge -- this mints a
      # short-lived token from a GitHub App installed on this repo instead.
      # See this pack's adoptNotes: if that's not this project's situation,
      # drop this step and pass `github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`
      # to the version step below instead. The App needs only
      # `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write`; its token auto-expires
      # in an hour and this action revokes it when the job ends.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        id: app-token
        with:
          # Both created as repo secrets (`gh secret set`), not vars: the
          # client ID isn't sensitive on its own, but keeping both next to
          # each other avoids a second place to remember to update.
          client-id: ${{ secrets.APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      - uses: changesets/action/version@ae32849d5ba541f9ae29e40e22a623bc13562f51 # v2
        with:
          github-token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          script: pnpm version:packages
          commit-message: "chore(release): version packages"
          pr-title: "chore(release): version packages"

  pack:
    name: Verify and pack
    needs: select-mode
    if: needs.select-mode.outputs.mode == 'publish'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    outputs:
      pack-dir-artifact-id: ${{ steps.pack.outputs.pack-dir-artifact-id }}
    permissions:
      contents: read # actions/checkout
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@73e46992e05b19abd31f2f3c20e0e7370d762115 # v6.1.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      # The whole gate, before a tarball exists. `pnpm verify` is one full
      # run of every group, the same steps ci.yml spreads across its lanes.
      - run: pnpm verify
      # Deliberately not one of pnpm verify's own steps: package.json's
      # version only changes in the version PR, so this check would fail
      # every ordinary push between releases (the version it's checking is
      # always the one already published) if it ran there. This is the one
      # place "is this version about to collide with an already-published
      # one" is the right question to ask -- right before packing it.
      - run: node bin/check-publish-version.mjs
      - id: pack
        uses: changesets/action/pack@ae32849d5ba541f9ae29e40e22a623bc13562f51 # v2
        with:
          publish-plan-artifact-id: ${{ needs.select-mode.outputs.publish-plan-artifact-id }}

  publish:
    name: Publish to npm
    needs: pack
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Gates the git tag, the GitHub Release, and the staged publish behind a
    # required reviewer -- without this, all three already exist by the time
    # a maintainer even sees there's a staged version to approve with
    # `npm stage approve`. The environment (created once, by hand, via
    # `gh api` -- see this pack's adoptNotes) has no branch restriction
    # beyond the release branch and no wait timer: it exists to require a
    # person, not to add a delay.
    environment: npm-publish
    permissions:
      contents: write # changesets/action/publish pushes tags and creates GitHub Releases
      id-token: write # npm trusted publishing (OIDC) and provenance
      attestations: write # actions/attest-build-provenance on the packed tarball
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@73e46992e05b19abd31f2f3c20e0e7370d762115 # v6.1.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      # Only the changesets CLI is needed here, not any package's lifecycle scripts.
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
      # Staged publishing goes through libnpmpublish (npm's own publish
      # library, bin/npm-stage-publish.mjs), not the npm CLI: the CLI bundles
      # its own dependencies, which no override can patch. Pinned to exact
      # versions, not a range or `latest`: this job holds the OIDC token, and
      # an unpinned package install is exactly what OpenSSF Scorecard's
      # Pinned-Dependencies check flags. `tools/release/` pins every tarball
      # via its committed lockfile's integrity hash, and `npm ci` verifies the
      # install against it -- bumping the pin is then a normal reviewed PR (a
      # lockfile diff), not a hand-edited version string.
      - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --prefix tools/release
      # changesets publishes through `pnpm publish` in a pnpm-managed
      # project. This puts a `pnpm` ahead of the real one that forwards
      # everything except `publish`, which goes to a staged publish
      # instead (see bin/pnpm-publish-shim.mjs -- the trusted publisher only
      # allows staged publishing, npm's own default since 2026-09-03).
      - name: Route publish through the staged publisher
        run: |
          shim_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/pnpm-shim"
          mkdir -p "$shim_dir"
          printf '#!/bin/sh\nexport PNPM_SHIM_DIR=%s\nexec node "%s/bin/pnpm-publish-shim.mjs" "$@"\n' \
            "$shim_dir" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" > "$shim_dir/pnpm"
          chmod +x "$shim_dir/pnpm"
          echo "$shim_dir" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - uses: changesets/action/publish@ae32849d5ba541f9ae29e40e22a623bc13562f51 # v2
        id: publish
        env:
          RELEASE_TOOLS_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/tools/release
          STAGED_IDS_FILE: ${{ runner.temp }}/staged-ids.txt
        with:
          pack-dir-artifact-id: ${{ needs.pack.outputs.pack-dir-artifact-id }}
      # changesets swallows the publisher's stdout, so the stage id to approve
      # would never reach this log. The publisher records it in a file; print
      # it here, plus an annotation on the run page, whether or not an earlier
      # step failed. `npm stage approve <id>` (2FA) is still a maintainer step.
      - name: Show the staged ids to approve
        if: always()
        env:
          STAGED_IDS_FILE: ${{ runner.temp }}/staged-ids.txt
        run: |
          if [ -s "$STAGED_IDS_FILE" ]; then
            while read -r id stage; do
              echo "staged $id with id $stage -- approve with: npm stage approve $stage"
              echo "::notice title=Staged $id::npm stage approve $stage"
            done < "$STAGED_IDS_FILE"
          else
            echo "no stage id was recorded by this run -- a version may still have been staged; check with: npm stage list"
            echo "::warning title=No stage id recorded::A version may still be staged. Run npm stage list before re-running."
          fi
      # npm provenance alone already meets most supply-chain "signed
      # releases" criteria (a Sigstore-backed, OIDC-issued attestation with
      # no long-lived key). These three steps add a second, independent
      # proof on the GitHub Release itself: the exact tarball `pack` already
      # built and tested, fetched back out of its own artifact (never
      # rebuilt), attested, and attached. `if:` guards all three on
      # `publish` actually having published -- `select-mode` only decides
      # the job should run, not that a version was new.
      # `continue-on-error: true` on all three: the staged publish has
      # already succeeded by this point, so a failure here (a transient
      # download error, say) must never fail the whole job and leave a
      # staged, tagged, unreleased version behind -- this block is
      # best-effort supplementary evidence. (The stage id to approve is
      # printed, and added to the job summary, by the publish step itself.)
      - name: Fetch the packed tarball back out of the pack job's artifact
        if: steps.publish.outputs.published == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          artifact-ids: ${{ needs.pack.outputs.pack-dir-artifact-id }}
          path: .release-artifacts
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: Attest build provenance for the published tarball
        if: steps.publish.outputs.published == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          # actions/attest-build-provenance's own glob support (not the
          # shell's), so `**` resolves correctly regardless of `globstar`.
          subject-path: .release-artifacts/**/*.tgz
      - name: Attach the attested tarball to the GitHub Release
        if: steps.publish.outputs.published == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          # `changeset pack` writes into <outDir>/packages/*.tgz, not
          # <outDir>/*.tgz -- found by path, not a bare shell glob the
          # default (non-globstar) bash would pass through unexpanded on
          # no match.
          tarball="$(find .release-artifacts -name '*.tgz' -print -quit)"
          if [ -z "$tarball" ]; then
            echo "no packed tarball found under .release-artifacts/ -- skipping the release-asset upload" >&2
            exit 0
          fi
          name="$(node -p "require('./package.json').name")"
          version="$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")"
          # changesets names the tag `v<version>` for a single-package
          # repository (its "root" tool, which is what this baseline is: no
          # `packages:` in pnpm-workspace.yaml) and `<name>@<version>` once
          # the repository becomes a workspace. Upload to whichever one
          # actually has a Release rather than guessing.
          tag=""
          for candidate in "v${version}" "${name}@${version}"; do
            if gh release view "$candidate" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              tag="$candidate"
              break
            fi
          done
          if [ -z "$tag" ]; then
            echo "cannot attach the tarball: no GitHub Release found for v${version} or ${name}@${version} -- failing this best-effort step" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          gh release upload "$tag" \
            "$tarball" --clobber --repo "${{ github.repository }}"

## What this is

**__PROJECT_NAME__** — a TypeScript project bootstrapped by

Run any task with `pnpm <script>`.

| Script                         | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                             |

| `pnpm typecheck`               | `tsc -b --force` over the tooling project (src + tests)                                                                                                                                                  |
| `pnpm lint`                    | ESLint over the whole repo                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `pnpm format` / `format:check` | Prettier write / check                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `pnpm test` / `test:coverage`  | Vitest, with or without the coverage gate                                                                                                                                                                |
| `pnpm knip`                    | Unused-dependency / unused-export hygiene; a `verify` step. `knip.json` ignores `@commitlint/config-conventional` and `@commitlint/types`, which are loaded by a string and a JSDoc type knip cannot see |

locally.

(`bin/lint-commit.mjs`, run after `bin/strip-claude-trailers.mjs` removes

authored or substantially assisted a commit — see `.claude/skills/writing-commits/`.

while `HEAD` is `main`. Land any `src/`/`tests/` change via PR. Run
`.claude/skills/starting-work/` before beginning change-work if you haven't
already settled the branch and PR decision.

`src/index.ts` is the current public entry point (see the `exports` map in
`package.json`). By convention, anything under `src/internal/` (if you create
it) is private and is not re-exported from the entry point; no lint rule
enforces this, so review for it.

`src/`/test code itself — enforced by `.claude/hooks/guard-hub-src-writes.mjs`

contract:

2. `code-implementer` makes them pass with the minimal correct

   until clean.

locating files and symbols.

- `writing-commits` — drafts a Conventional Commit from the staged diff.
- `creating-prs` — verifies gates, pushes, opens the PR and picks a merge path.
- `triaging-ci` — diagnoses a failed CI run and proposes fixes.
- `finishing-work` — post-merge cleanup: branches, refs, work log.

  sweeps (see Freshness).

runs on every `Bash` call and blocks a command that visibly writes into
`src/` or `tests/` (redirects, `tee`, `sed -i`, `cp`/`mv` into them, a

file, an `eval`, a computed path, a parent of the project root (`rm -rf ..`), a workspace container below the project root (`tools/packages/foo`), a build step, a formatter or fixer

`!` prefix at the Claude Code prompt, or edit the hook's registration in
`.claude/settings.json`.

silently disable it.** Managed settings (a `managed-settings.json` file, an
MDM policy, or a claude.ai-console-managed remote policy) take precedence
over every file this baseline installs, with no project-level override, and
two managed-only keys -- `allowManagedHooksOnly` and
`allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` -- mean that only managed hooks run
(`allowManagedHooksOnly`) and only managed permission rules apply
(`allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`) (see

repo -- the managed file lives outside any working tree, at an OS-level
path. Run `/status` on a machine you don't control before trusting

handles `tool.check` "can approve a call that your `PreToolUse` hook blocked,
unless the hook is in managed settings", and project `PreToolUse` hooks run
only after the last mod calls `next` (see the
[mods events reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/events)).

one. Check `/plugin` for installed mods alongside `/status`.

writer spoke only with both present, so a call carrying `agent_type` but no
`agent_id` is treated as the hub and is blocked.

`settings.json`.** `guard-secret-writes`, `guard-hub-src-writes`,
`guard-branch-isolation` and `guard-protected-paths` carry
`"onFailure": "block"` (Claude Code 2.1.295 or later). By default a hook that
crashes or times out lets the call through; with this key it is blocked. It
applies only to a failure the hook does not handle itself: each guard still
catches bad input and exits 0 on purpose, so the key covers a load error, a
missing `node` or the 30-second timeout. Because `guard-hub-src-writes` is also
registered on `Bash`, a missing `node` or a timed-out scan blocks every `Bash`
call until it is fixed (run the command yourself with the `!` prefix to get
past it). The style guards and `guard-git-push-signed` stay fail-open on
purpose: the push guard has its own command parser and the remote's
signed-commit rule is the authoritative layer. `permissions.deny` blocks
`Read(./.env)`, `Read(./.env.*)` and `Read(./secrets/**)`, which also covers
`cat`, `head` and `tail` on those files in `Bash`. It does not cover `grep -r`
or a script that opens the file itself, and nothing else in this baseline does.

**A spoke's `permissionMode` can be overridden.** A session in auto,
`acceptEdits` or `bypassPermissions` mode overrides a spoke's `permissionMode`
(the field applies only when the session is in `default`, `dontAsk` or
`plan`), so treat the hooks, not `permissionMode`, as what bounds a spoke.
Claude Code also lets a subagent spawn subagents three layers deep by default;
`disallowedTools: Agent` on every spoke is what keeps this roster flat.

Full dispatch-sizing and recovery guidance: `.claude/rules/agent-dispatch.md`
(auto-loads when editing `.claude/skills/**` or `.claude/agents/**`).

## Coding, errors & tests

Path-scoped rules auto-load on matching files:

- `src/**` → `.claude/rules/src.md`
- `**/tests/**`, `**/*.test.ts` → `.claude/rules/tests.md`
- `src/**`, `**/tests/**` → `.claude/rules/refactoring.md` (behavior-preserving changes)
- `.claude/skills/**`, `.claude/agents/**` → `.claude/rules/agent-dispatch.md`

## Security

Never log secrets, tokens, or caller data. Validate external input at the
public API boundary. `.claude/hooks/guard-secret-writes.mjs` blocks writing
a real secret to disk at edit time; keep it that way rather than relying on
CI to catch it after the fact.

## Definition of Done

`pnpm verify` passes; a public API change carries a Conventional Commit with
the correct semver impact; new/changed exports have TSDoc and tests. If you
touched the harness itself (hooks, agents, skills, rules, `settings.json`),

fails on broken wiring and only warns on quality.
The `toolchain` step (`bin/check-toolchain.mjs`) runs on every

deprecated). Never silence it by deleting the check or lowering a threshold --
fix the config it points at.

## Forbidden Patterns

**Enforced at write time by hooks:** `any` implied by CommonJS constructs
(`require`, `module.exports`, `__dirname`, `__filename`), a missing `.js`
extension on a relative import, a hand-edit to `dist/` or `coverage/`, a
write to `src/`/`tests/` while on `main`, a real secret written to disk,
an unsigned `git push` when `commit.gpgsign` is on, and a `run_in_background`
Bash call stacked with a shell-level detach construct.

**No automated guard — need conscious care:** no `any` in the public API;
never swallow an error silently; no top-level side effects; never
`git push --force`.

## Freshness

This baseline is frozen at the moment `m3l-groundwork` last emitted it. Run
`/customize`'s guidance pass — or `.claude/skills/typescript-guidance/` /
`.claude/skills/harness-guidance/` directly in refresh mode — periodically
to sweep the toolchain and harness against current upstream guidance; its
`gaps` mode recommends tooling the project doesn't have yet. See
`docs/research/typescript-refresh.md` and `docs/research/harness-refresh.md`
for the living trackers.

| `pnpm lint`                    | ESLint over the whole repo                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `pnpm format` / `format:check` | Prettier write / check                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `pnpm test` / `test:coverage`  | Vitest, with or without the coverage gate                                                                                                                                                                |
| `pnpm knip`                    | Unused-dependency / unused-export hygiene; a `verify` step. `knip.json` ignores `@commitlint/config-conventional` and `@commitlint/types`, which are loaded by a string and a JSDoc type knip cannot see |
| `pnpm check:exports`           | publint + are-the-types-wrong against a packed tarball                                                                                                                                                   |
| `pnpm check:node-version`      | `.node-version` is authoritative; forbids a hardcoded pin in CI                                                                                                                                          |
| `pnpm verify`                  | Every gate above plus the `harness`/`toolchain` graders, in `verify-steps.mjs` order; CI runs them as five parallel group lanes                                                                          |
| `pnpm prepare`                 | Installs the lefthook git hooks                                                                                                                                                                          |

Run `pnpm verify` before considering any task done — it reproduces CI
locally.

## Git Workflow

**Conventional Commits (required)**, enforced by the `commit-msg` hook
(`bin/lint-commit.mjs`, run after `bin/strip-claude-trailers.mjs` removes
harness-injected `Claude-*` trailers). Add a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer when Claude
authored or substantially assisted a commit — see `.claude/skills/writing-commits/`.

Branch off `main` as `feat/<slug>` / `fix/<slug>`, never work directly on
`main` — `guard-branch-isolation.mjs` blocks `src/**`/`tests/**` writes
while `HEAD` is `main`. Land any `src/`/`tests/` change via PR. Run
`.claude/skills/starting-work/` before beginning change-work if you haven't
already settled the branch and PR decision.

Never `git push --force` a shared branch.

## Architecture & Decisions

`src/index.ts` is the current public entry point (see the `exports` map in
`package.json`). By convention, anything under `src/internal/` (if you create
it) is private and is not re-exported from the entry point; no lint rule
enforces this, so review for it.

## Agent Operating Model

**Hub-and-spoke**: the hub plans and dispatches to spokes, and never writes
`src/`/test code itself — enforced by `.claude/hooks/guard-hub-src-writes.mjs`
and `disallowedTools: Agent` on every spoke. For a piece of work with a clear
contract:

1. `test-author` writes failing tests from the contract (RED phase), and
   confirms they fail for the right reason.
2. `code-implementer` makes them pass with the minimal correct
   implementation, then refactors while green (GREEN phase).
3. Read-only review spokes (`code-reviewer` always; `silent-failure-hunter`
   when the diff has error-handling paths) run in parallel over the diff.
   Must-fix findings route back to `code-implementer`, and the loop repeats
   until clean.

Also shipped: `.claude/agents/Explore.md`, a fast read-only search agent for
locating files and symbols.

Skills, each in `.claude/skills/<name>/`:

- `starting-work` — pre-work gate: picks the branch and whether a PR is needed.
- `writing-commits` — drafts a Conventional Commit from the staged diff.
- `creating-prs` — verifies gates, pushes, opens the PR and picks a merge path.
- `triaging-ci` — diagnoses a failed CI run and proposes fixes.
- `finishing-work` — post-merge cleanup: branches, refs, work log.
- `typescript-guidance` / `harness-guidance` — live research and refresh
  sweeps (see Freshness).

**The guard also screens `Bash`, but only conservatively.** The same hook
blocks a `Bash` command that visibly writes into `src/` or `tests/` (redirects,
`tee`, `sed -i`, `cp`/`mv` into them, an interpreter snippet that writes there,
a copy, move or removal of a parent of `src/` such as `rm -rf .`) unless the caller is
`test-author` or `code-implementer`. It cannot catch an indirect write (a
script from a project file, an `eval`, a computed path, a build step, a
formatter or fixer, `git rm`/`git mv`, `tar`/`curl -o`), so hub-and-spoke is a
convention backed by a guard that raises the bar, not a proof. To override it
deliberately, run the command yourself with the `!` prefix at the Claude Code
prompt, or edit the hook's registration in `.claude/settings.json`.

**Managed settings and mods can silently disable the guards.** A managed
deployment (`managed-settings.json`, MDM, a console policy) outranks every file
here, and `allowManagedHooksOnly` runs only managed hooks. An installed mod
that handles `tool.check` can approve a call a project `PreToolUse` hook
blocked, and only managed hooks outrank a mod. Nothing in the repo can detect
either: on a machine you don't control, check `/status` ("Setting sources") and
`/plugin` before trusting `guard-hub-src-writes.mjs` and
`guard-branch-isolation.mjs`. Detail and sources:
`.claude/rules/agent-dispatch.md`.

**The guard keys on `agent_id` as well as `agent_type`.** A call counts as a
writer spoke only with both present, so one carrying `agent_type` alone is
treated as the hub and blocked, as is a fork subagent unless its payload
reports a writer `agent_type` with an `agent_id` (details and versions in
`.claude/rules/agent-dispatch.md`). An in-process
agent-teams teammate has a documented `agent_id`, so one built from a writer
definition that reports that `agent_type` would pass.

**Four guards block when they fail, and a secrets deny rule ships in
`settings.json`.** `guard-secret-writes`, `guard-hub-src-writes`,
`guard-branch-isolation` and `guard-protected-paths` carry
`"onFailure": "block"` (Claude Code 2.1.295 or later): a hook that cannot
start, times out, exits with any code other than 0 or 2, or prints invalid
JSON blocks the call instead of letting it through. Each guard still handles
bad input itself and exits 0 on purpose. Because `guard-hub-src-writes` is also
on `Bash`, a missing `node` blocks every `Bash` call until fixed (run the
command with the `!` prefix to get past it). The style guards and
`guard-git-push-signed` stay fail-open on purpose: the push guard has its own
parser and the remote's signed-commit rule is the authoritative layer.
`permissions.deny` blocks `Read(./.env)`, `Read(./.env.*)` and
`Read(./secrets/**)`, which also covers `cat`, `head` and `tail` on them in
`Bash`. It does not cover `grep -r` or a script that opens the file itself.

**A spoke's `permissionMode` can be overridden.** A session in auto,
`acceptEdits` or `bypassPermissions` mode overrides a spoke's `permissionMode`
(the field applies only in `default`, `dontAsk` or `plan`), so the hooks, not
`permissionMode`, bound a spoke. A subagent can spawn subagents three layers
deep by default; `disallowedTools: Agent` on every spoke keeps the roster flat.

Full dispatch-sizing and recovery guidance: `.claude/rules/agent-dispatch.md`
(auto-loads when editing `.claude/skills/**` or `.claude/agents/**`).

## Coding, errors & tests

Path-scoped rules auto-load on matching files:

- `src/**` → `.claude/rules/src.md`
- `**/tests/**`, `**/*.test.ts` → `.claude/rules/tests.md`
- `src/**`, `**/tests/**` → `.claude/rules/refactoring.md` (behavior-preserving changes)
- `.claude/skills/**`, `.claude/agents/**` → `.claude/rules/agent-dispatch.md`

## Security

Never log secrets, tokens, or caller data. Validate external input at the
public API boundary. `.claude/hooks/guard-secret-writes.mjs` blocks writing
a real secret to disk at edit time; keep it that way rather than relying on
CI to catch it after the fact.

## Definition of Done

`pnpm verify` passes; a public API change carries a Conventional Commit with
the correct semver impact; new/changed exports have TSDoc and tests. If you
touched the harness itself (hooks, agents, skills, rules, `settings.json`),
`pnpm verify`'s `harness` step (`bin/check-harness.mjs`) must stay green: it
fails on broken wiring and only warns on quality.
The `toolchain` step (`bin/check-toolchain.mjs`) runs on every
`pnpm verify`, and must stay green when you touch the TypeScript toolchain
(`tsconfig*.json`, `eslint.config.js`, `vitest.config.ts`,
`bin/lib/verify-steps.mjs`, the toolchain pins in `package.json`) the same way: it fails on wiring `tsc` and ESLint do not catch (a build
project that emits nowhere, a verify step naming a script that does not exist)
and only warns on quality (a missing strict flag, an option TypeScript has
deprecated). Never silence it by deleting the check or lowering a threshold --
fix the config it points at.

## Forbidden Patterns

**Enforced at write time by hooks:** `any` implied by CommonJS constructs
(`require`, `module.exports`, `__dirname`, `__filename`), a missing `.js`
extension on a relative import, a hand-edit to `dist/` or `coverage/`, a
write to `src/`/`tests/` while on `main`, a real secret written to disk,
an unsigned `git push` when `commit.gpgsign` is on, and a `run_in_background`
Bash call stacked with a shell-level detach construct.

**No automated guard — need conscious care:** no `any` in the public API;
never swallow an error silently; no top-level side effects; never
`git push --force`.

## Freshness

This baseline is frozen at the moment `m3l-groundwork` last emitted it. Run
`/customize`'s guidance pass — or `.claude/skills/typescript-guidance/` /
`.claude/skills/harness-guidance/` directly in refresh mode — periodically
to sweep the toolchain and harness against current upstream guidance; its
`gaps` mode recommends tooling the project doesn't have yet. See
`docs/research/typescript-refresh.md` and `docs/research/harness-refresh.md`
for the living trackers.

name: Release

# What this does: on every push to `main`, this workflow either opens a PR
# that bumps the package version and changelog, or -- once that PR has
# merged -- packs and publishes the package to npm. It runs
# [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets), the tool this
# project uses to track pending releases (each PR that changes the
# package's user-facing behavior adds a small Markdown file under
# `.changeset/` describing the change and its version bump; this workflow
# reads those files to decide what to do next).
#
# The flow, one job each:
#   1. select-mode  reads the repo and decides: "version", "publish", or "none"
#   2. version      opens or updates the "Version Packages" PR
#   3. pack         builds, runs every gate, and packs the tarball
#   4. publish      uploads that tarball to npm via trusted publishing
#
# "Trusted publishing" is npm's passwordless publish mechanism: instead of a
# long-lived npm token stored as a secret, this workflow proves its identity
# to npm via OIDC (OpenID Connect -- a short-lived, cryptographically signed
# token GitHub Actions mints for the running job, which npm verifies against
# the trusted-publisher config for this exact repo and workflow file). This
# is the shape the changesets docs recommend for trusted publishing: the one
# job that holds the OIDC token (`publish`, via `id-token: write`) never runs
# build, test, or repo-script code -- it only runs the changesets CLI and the
# pnpm shim below, with `--ignore-scripts`. `pack` holds nothing beyond
# `contents: read`.
#
# "Staged" publish (vs. a "direct" one) means a staged publish uploads the
# tarball and creates the version, but it isn't installable yet until a
# maintainer separately approves it with 2FA (`npm stage approve`) -- npm's
# own stronger default over a direct `npm publish`, which would make the
# version live immediately. "Provenance" is the signed, publicly verifiable
# record npm attaches to a trusted-published package, linking it back to the
# exact commit and workflow run that built it.
#
# npm trusted publishers are configured per package, against this exact file
# name (`release.yml`, not a path) -- see this pack's adoptNotes for the
# one-time setup this depends on.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

# Reset, then grant per job.
permissions: {}

# Releases must not be cancelled midway: a half-published release is worse
# than a queued one.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}

jobs:
  select-mode:
    name: Select mode
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    outputs:
      mode: ${{ steps.select-mode.outputs.mode }}
      publish-plan-artifact-id: ${{ steps.select-mode.outputs.publish-plan-artifact-id }}
    permissions:
      contents: read # actions/checkout
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      # `.node-version` is the single Node pin, so this file must never carry
      # a literal version (see check-node-version.mjs). No package-manager
      # cache anywhere in this file: a restored cache is an input an attacker
      # can poison, and these jobs are the ones that publish.
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@ea17c68df8912ef543352723c149a84f56e3d413 # v6.1.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - id: select-mode
        uses: changesets/action/select-mode@ae32849d5ba541f9ae29e40e22a623bc13562f51 # v2

  version:
    name: Open version PR
    needs: select-mode
    if: needs.select-mode.outputs.mode == 'version'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read # actions/checkout; see below for who does the actual writing
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@ea17c68df8912ef543352723c149a84f56e3d413 # v6.1.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      # If this project's branch protection requires status checks on every
      # PR with no bypass actor, a PR opened with the default GITHUB_TOKEN
      # never triggers `pull_request`-event workflows (GitHub's own
      # anti-recursion rule) and could therefore never merge -- this mints a
      # short-lived token from a GitHub App installed on this repo instead.
      # See this pack's adoptNotes: if that's not this project's situation,
      # drop this step and pass `github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`
      # to the version step below instead. The App needs only
      # `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write`; its token auto-expires
      # in an hour and this action revokes it when the job ends.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        with:
          # Both created as repo secrets (`gh secret set`), not vars: the
          # client ID isn't sensitive on its own, but keeping both next to
          # each other avoids a second place to remember to update.
          client-id: ${{ secrets.APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      - uses: changesets/action/version@ae32849d5ba541f9ae29e40e22a623bc13562f51 # v2
        with:
          github-token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          script: pnpm version:packages
          commit-message: "chore(release): version packages"
          pr-title: "chore(release): version packages"

  pack:
    name: Verify and pack
    needs: select-mode
    if: needs.select-mode.outputs.mode == 'publish'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    outputs:
      pack-dir-artifact-id: ${{ steps.pack.outputs.pack-dir-artifact-id }}
    permissions:
      contents: read # actions/checkout
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@ea17c68df8912ef543352723c149a84f56e3d413 # v6.1.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      # The whole gate, before a tarball exists. `pnpm verify` is one full
      # run of every group, the same steps ci.yml spreads across its lanes.
      - run: pnpm verify
      # Deliberately not one of pnpm verify's own steps: package.json's
      # version only changes in the version PR, so this check would fail
      # every ordinary push between releases (the version it's checking is
      # always the one already published) if it ran there. This is the one
      # place "is this version about to collide with an already-published
      # one" is the right question to ask -- right before packing it.
      - run: node bin/check-publish-version.mjs
      - id: pack
        uses: changesets/action/pack@ae32849d5ba541f9ae29e40e22a623bc13562f51 # v2
        with:
          publish-plan-artifact-id: ${{ needs.select-mode.outputs.publish-plan-artifact-id }}

  publish:
    name: Publish to npm
    needs: pack
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Gates the git tag, the GitHub Release, and the staged publish behind a
    # required reviewer -- without this, all three already exist by the time
    # a maintainer even sees there's a staged version to approve with
    # `npm stage approve`. The environment (created once, by hand, via
    # `gh api` -- see this pack's adoptNotes) has no branch restriction
    # beyond the release branch and no wait timer: it exists to require a
    # person, not to add a delay.
    environment: npm-publish
    permissions:
      contents: write # changesets/action/publish pushes tags and creates GitHub Releases
      id-token: write # npm trusted publishing (OIDC) and provenance
      attestations: write # actions/attest-build-provenance on the packed tarball
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@ea17c68df8912ef543352723c149a84f56e3d413 # v6.1.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      # Only the changesets CLI is needed here, not any package's lifecycle scripts.
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
      # Staged publishing goes through libnpmpublish (npm's own publish
      # library, bin/npm-stage-publish.mjs), not the npm CLI: the CLI bundles
      # its own dependencies, which no override can patch. Pinned to exact
      # versions, not a range or `latest`: this job holds the OIDC token, and
      # an unpinned package install is exactly what OpenSSF Scorecard's
      # Pinned-Dependencies check flags. `tools/release/` pins every tarball
      # via its committed lockfile's integrity hash, and `npm ci` verifies the
      # install against it -- bumping the pin is then a normal reviewed PR (a
      # lockfile diff), not a hand-edited version string.
      - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --prefix tools/release
      # changesets publishes through `pnpm publish` in a pnpm-managed
      # project. This puts a `pnpm` ahead of the real one that forwards
      # everything except `publish`, which goes to a staged publish
      # instead (see bin/pnpm-publish-shim.mjs -- the trusted publisher only
      # allows staged publishing, npm's own default since 2026-09-03).
      - name: Route publish through the staged publisher
        run: |
          shim_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/pnpm-shim"
          mkdir -p "$shim_dir"
          printf '#!/bin/sh\nexport PNPM_SHIM_DIR=%s\nexec node "%s/bin/pnpm-publish-shim.mjs" "$@"\n' \
            "$shim_dir" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" > "$shim_dir/pnpm"
          chmod +x "$shim_dir/pnpm"
          echo "$shim_dir" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - uses: changesets/action/publish@ae32849d5ba541f9ae29e40e22a623bc13562f51 # v2
        id: publish
        env:
          RELEASE_TOOLS_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/tools/release
          STAGED_IDS_FILE: ${{ runner.temp }}/staged-ids.txt
        with:
          pack-dir-artifact-id: ${{ needs.pack.outputs.pack-dir-artifact-id }}
      # changesets swallows the publisher's stdout, so the stage id to approve
      # would never reach this log. The publisher records it in a file; print
      # it here, plus an annotation on the run page, whether or not an earlier
      # step failed. `npm stage approve <id>` (2FA) is still a maintainer step.
      - name: Show the staged ids to approve
        if: always()
        env:
          STAGED_IDS_FILE: ${{ runner.temp }}/staged-ids.txt
        run: |
          if [ -s "$STAGED_IDS_FILE" ]; then
            while read -r id stage; do
              echo "staged $id with id $stage -- approve with: npm stage approve $stage"
              echo "::notice title=Staged $id::npm stage approve $stage"
            done < "$STAGED_IDS_FILE"
          else
            echo "no staged version was recorded by this run"
          fi
      # npm provenance alone already meets most supply-chain "signed
      # releases" criteria (a Sigstore-backed, OIDC-issued attestation with
      # no long-lived key). These three steps add a second, independent
      # proof on the GitHub Release itself: the exact tarball `pack` already
      # built and tested, fetched back out of its own artifact (never
      # rebuilt), attested, and attached. `if:` guards all three on
      # `publish` actually having published -- `select-mode` only decides
      # the job should run, not that a version was new.
      # `continue-on-error: true` on all three: the staged publish has
      # already succeeded by this point, so a failure here (a transient
      # download error, say) must never fail the whole job and leave a
      # staged, tagged, unreleased version behind -- this block is
      # best-effort supplementary evidence. (The stage id to approve is
      # printed, and added to the job summary, by the publish step itself.)
      - name: Fetch the packed tarball back out of the pack job's artifact
        if: steps.publish.outputs.published == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          artifact-ids: ${{ needs.pack.outputs.pack-dir-artifact-id }}
          path: .release-artifacts
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: Attest build provenance for the published tarball
        if: steps.publish.outputs.published == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          # actions/attest-build-provenance's own glob support (not the
          # shell's), so `**` resolves correctly regardless of `globstar`.
          subject-path: .release-artifacts/**/*.tgz
      - name: Attach the attested tarball to the GitHub Release
        if: steps.publish.outputs.published == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          # `changeset pack` writes into <outDir>/packages/*.tgz, not
          # <outDir>/*.tgz -- found by path, not a bare shell glob the
          # default (non-globstar) bash would pass through unexpanded on
          # no match.
          tarball="$(find .release-artifacts -name '*.tgz' -print -quit)"
          if [ -z "$tarball" ]; then
            echo "no packed tarball found under .release-artifacts/ -- skipping the release-asset upload" >&2
            exit 0
          fi
          name="$(node -p "require('./package.json').name")"
          version="$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")"
          # changesets names the tag `v<version>` for a single-package
          # repository (its "root" tool, which is what this baseline is: no
          # `packages:` in pnpm-workspace.yaml) and `<name>@<version>` once
          # the repository becomes a workspace. Upload to whichever one
          # actually has a Release rather than guessing.
          tag=""
          for candidate in "v${version}" "${name}@${version}"; do
            if gh release view "$candidate" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              tag="$candidate"
              break
            fi
          done
          if [ -z "$tag" ]; then
            echo "cannot attach the tarball: no GitHub Release found for v${version} or ${name}@${version} -- failing this best-effort step" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          gh release upload "$tag" \
            "$tarball" --clobber --repo "${{ github.repository }}"

# is the shape the changesets docs recommend for trusted publishing: the one
# job that holds the OIDC token (`publish`, via `id-token: write`) never runs
# build, test, or repo-script code -- it only runs the changesets CLI and the
# pnpm shim below, with `--ignore-scripts`. `pack` holds nothing beyond
# `contents: read`.
#
# "Staged" publish (vs. a "direct" one) means a staged publish uploads the
# tarball and creates the version, but it isn't installable yet until a
# maintainer separately approves it with 2FA (`npm stage approve`) -- npm's
# own stronger default over a direct `npm publish`, which would make the
# version live immediately. "Provenance" is the signed, publicly verifiable
# record npm attaches to a trusted-published package, linking it back to the
# exact commit and workflow run that built it.
#
# npm trusted publishers are configured per package, against this exact file
# name (`release.yml`, not a path) -- see this pack's adoptNotes for the
# one-time setup this depends on.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

# Reset, then grant per job.
permissions: {}

# Releases must not be cancelled midway: a half-published release is worse
# than a queued one.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}

jobs:
  select-mode:
    name: Select mode
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    outputs:
      mode: ${{ steps.select-mode.outputs.mode }}
      publish-plan-artifact-id: ${{ steps.select-mode.outputs.publish-plan-artifact-id }}
    permissions:
      contents: read # actions/checkout
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      # `.node-version` is the single Node pin, so this file must never carry
      # a literal version (see check-node-version.mjs). No package-manager
      # cache anywhere in this file: a restored cache is an input an attacker
      # can poison, and these jobs are the ones that publish.
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@73e46992e05b19abd31f2f3c20e0e7370d762115 # v6.1.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - id: select-mode
        uses: changesets/action/select-mode@ae32849d5ba541f9ae29e40e22a623bc13562f51 # v2

  version:
    name: Open version PR
    needs: select-mode
    if: needs.select-mode.outputs.mode == 'version'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read # actions/checkout; see below for who does the actual writing
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@73e46992e05b19abd31f2f3c20e0e7370d762115 # v6.1.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      # If this project's branch protection requires status checks on every
      # PR with no bypass actor, a PR opened with the default GITHUB_TOKEN
      # never triggers `pull_request`-event workflows (GitHub's own
      # anti-recursion rule) and could therefore never merge -- this mints a
      # short-lived token from a GitHub App installed on this repo instead.
      # See this pack's adoptNotes: if that's not this project's situation,
      # drop this step and pass `github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`
      # to the version step below instead. The App needs only
      # `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write`; its token auto-expires
      # in an hour and this action revokes it when the job ends.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        id: app-token
        with:
          # Both created as repo secrets (`gh secret set`), not vars: the
          # client ID isn't sensitive on its own, but keeping both next to
          # each other avoids a second place to remember to update.
          client-id: ${{ secrets.APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      - uses: changesets/action/version@ae32849d5ba541f9ae29e40e22a623bc13562f51 # v2
        with:
          github-token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          script: pnpm version:packages
          commit-message: "chore(release): version packages"
          pr-title: "chore(release): version packages"

  pack:
    name: Verify and pack
    needs: select-mode
    if: needs.select-mode.outputs.mode == 'publish'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    outputs:
      pack-dir-artifact-id: ${{ steps.pack.outputs.pack-dir-artifact-id }}
    permissions:
      contents: read # actions/checkout
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@73e46992e05b19abd31f2f3c20e0e7370d762115 # v6.1.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      # The whole gate, before a tarball exists. `pnpm verify` is one full
      # run of every group, the same steps ci.yml spreads across its lanes.
      - run: pnpm verify
      # Deliberately not one of pnpm verify's own steps: package.json's
      # version only changes in the version PR, so this check would fail
      # every ordinary push between releases (the version it's checking is
      # always the one already published) if it ran there. This is the one
      # place "is this version about to collide with an already-published
      # one" is the right question to ask -- right before packing it.
      - run: node bin/check-publish-version.mjs
      - id: pack
        uses: changesets/action/pack@ae32849d5ba541f9ae29e40e22a623bc13562f51 # v2
        with:
          publish-plan-artifact-id: ${{ needs.select-mode.outputs.publish-plan-artifact-id }}

  publish:
    name: Publish to npm
    needs: pack
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Gates the git tag, the GitHub Release, and the staged publish behind a
    # required reviewer -- without this, all three already exist by the time
    # a maintainer even sees there's a staged version to approve with
    # `npm stage approve`. The environment (created once, by hand, via
    # `gh api` -- see this pack's adoptNotes) has no branch restriction
    # beyond the release branch and no wait timer: it exists to require a
    # person, not to add a delay.
    environment: npm-publish
    permissions:
      contents: write # changesets/action/publish pushes tags and creates GitHub Releases
      id-token: write # npm trusted publishing (OIDC) and provenance
      attestations: write # actions/attest-build-provenance on the packed tarball
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@73e46992e05b19abd31f2f3c20e0e7370d762115 # v6.1.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      # Only the changesets CLI is needed here, not any package's lifecycle scripts.
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
      # Staged publishing goes through libnpmpublish (npm's own publish
      # library, bin/npm-stage-publish.mjs), not the npm CLI: the CLI bundles
      # its own dependencies, which no override can patch. Pinned to exact
      # versions, not a range or `latest`: this job holds the OIDC token, and
      # an unpinned package install is exactly what OpenSSF Scorecard's
      # Pinned-Dependencies check flags. `tools/release/` pins every tarball
      # via its committed lockfile's integrity hash, and `npm ci` verifies the
      # install against it -- bumping the pin is then a normal reviewed PR (a
      # lockfile diff), not a hand-edited version string.
      - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --prefix tools/release
      # changesets publishes through `pnpm publish` in a pnpm-managed
      # project. This puts a `pnpm` ahead of the real one that forwards
      # everything except `publish`, which goes to a staged publish
      # instead (see bin/pnpm-publish-shim.mjs -- the trusted publisher only
      # allows staged publishing, npm's own default since 2026-09-03).
      - name: Route publish through the staged publisher
        run: |
          shim_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/pnpm-shim"
          mkdir -p "$shim_dir"
          printf '#!/bin/sh\nexport PNPM_SHIM_DIR=%s\nexec node "%s/bin/pnpm-publish-shim.mjs" "$@"\n' \
            "$shim_dir" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" > "$shim_dir/pnpm"
          chmod +x "$shim_dir/pnpm"
          echo "$shim_dir" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - uses: changesets/action/publish@ae32849d5ba541f9ae29e40e22a623bc13562f51 # v2
        id: publish
        env:
          RELEASE_TOOLS_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/tools/release
          STAGED_IDS_FILE: ${{ runner.temp }}/staged-ids.txt
        with:
          pack-dir-artifact-id: ${{ needs.pack.outputs.pack-dir-artifact-id }}
      # changesets swallows the publisher's stdout, so the stage id to approve
      # would never reach this log. The publisher records it in a file; print
      # it here, plus an annotation on the run page, whether or not an earlier
      # step failed. `npm stage approve <id>` (2FA) is still a maintainer step.
      - name: Show the staged ids to approve
        if: always()
        env:
          STAGED_IDS_FILE: ${{ runner.temp }}/staged-ids.txt
        run: |
          if [ -s "$STAGED_IDS_FILE" ]; then
            while read -r id stage; do
              echo "staged $id with id $stage -- approve with: npm stage approve $stage"
              echo "::notice title=Staged $id::npm stage approve $stage"
            done < "$STAGED_IDS_FILE"
          else
            echo "no staged version was recorded by this run"
          fi
      # npm provenance alone already meets most supply-chain "signed
      # releases" criteria (a Sigstore-backed, OIDC-issued attestation with
      # no long-lived key). These three steps add a second, independent
      # proof on the GitHub Release itself: the exact tarball `pack` already
      # built and tested, fetched back out of its own artifact (never
      # rebuilt), attested, and attached. `if:` guards all three on
      # `publish` actually having published -- `select-mode` only decides
      # the job should run, not that a version was new.
      # `continue-on-error: true` on all three: the staged publish has
      # already succeeded by this point, so a failure here (a transient
      # download error, say) must never fail the whole job and leave a
      # staged, tagged, unreleased version behind -- this block is
      # best-effort supplementary evidence. (The stage id to approve is
      # printed, and added to the job summary, by the publish step itself.)
      - name: Fetch the packed tarball back out of the pack job's artifact
        if: steps.publish.outputs.published == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          artifact-ids: ${{ needs.pack.outputs.pack-dir-artifact-id }}
          path: .release-artifacts
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: Attest build provenance for the published tarball
        if: steps.publish.outputs.published == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          # actions/attest-build-provenance's own glob support (not the
          # shell's), so `**` resolves correctly regardless of `globstar`.
          subject-path: .release-artifacts/**/*.tgz
      - name: Attach the attested tarball to the GitHub Release
        if: steps.publish.outputs.published == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          # `changeset pack` writes into <outDir>/packages/*.tgz, not
          # <outDir>/*.tgz -- found by path, not a bare shell glob the
          # default (non-globstar) bash would pass through unexpanded on
          # no match.
          tarball="$(find .release-artifacts -name '*.tgz' -print -quit)"
          if [ -z "$tarball" ]; then
            echo "no packed tarball found under .release-artifacts/ -- skipping the release-asset upload" >&2
            exit 0
          fi
          name="$(node -p "require('./package.json').name")"
          version="$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")"
          # changesets names the tag `v<version>` for a single-package
          # repository (its "root" tool, which is what this baseline is: no
          # `packages:` in pnpm-workspace.yaml) and `<name>@<version>` once
          # the repository becomes a workspace. Upload to whichever one
          # actually has a Release rather than guessing.
          tag=""
          for candidate in "v${version}" "${name}@${version}"; do
            if gh release view "$candidate" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              tag="$candidate"
              break
            fi
          done
          if [ -z "$tag" ]; then
            echo "cannot attach the tarball: no GitHub Release found for v${version} or ${name}@${version} -- failing this best-effort step" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          gh release upload "$tag" \
            "$tarball" --clobber --repo "${{ github.repository }}"
